# Kaleidoscope

> Local native memory for agents, exposed through a manager CLI and persistent stdio MCP. Release status: staging (unreleased); no package or production login is public.

- [Documentation](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/): product and developer overview
- [Getting started](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/getting-started/): release-gated profile and reversible host workflow
- [CLI reference](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/cli/): exact local manager-candidate commands
- [MCP reference](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/mcp/): candidate-bound `search` and `remember` contract
- [Integrations](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/integrations/): Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, and generic MCP
- [Security](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/security/): package, process, and account isolation evidence
- [Privacy](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/privacy/): local/account data boundary, credential storage, and telemetry status
- [Account](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/account/): login manages account/device state and does not upload local memory
- [Operations](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/operations/): backup, restore, uninstall, update, and exact vault deletion
- [Compatibility](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/compatibility/): verified local cells versus native/support holds
- [Benchmarks](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/benchmarks/): merged candidate-bound smoke, with no score or release claim
- [Release evidence](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/evidence/): exact digests, milestone commits, rebind requirement, and protected gates
- [Public agent skill](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/SKILL.md): bounded retrieval and verified durable writes
- [Agent instructions](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/agent-instructions.md): safe manager-installed AGENTS, CLAUDE, and Cursor pointers
- [Machine-readable staging evidence](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/staging-evidence.json): source-free milestone and gate record
- [Candidate CLI help](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/reference/kaleidoscope-cli.candidate.txt): exact DX-05B manager help snapshot
- [Candidate MCP reference](https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/reference/kaleidoscope-mcp.candidate.json): exact engine and public-contract binding plus tool fields

The engine remains proprietary object code and its source is not in the public surfaces. The manager, wrappers, integrations, skill, and original documentation have no approved public license grant yet. The locally verified engine candidate SHA-256 is 988192ac9677d5dd55a3642b2da493a0806bb860b5b3c0f509b37ddadee08825; its public-contract SHA-256 is a2357ed6c00e3e143d08581590571447e31d24fd0e7d2466d28a211a0515c75e. The final auth-merged manager and regenerated distribution digests do not exist yet. Hosted memory is planned, not available. Production publication, login, and Pages promotion require separate approval.

# Kaleidoscope documentation

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Kaleidoscope is local memory for agents: a native CLI and persistent stdio MCP server with one profile shared across configured harnesses.

Release status. This is a non-indexable documentation staging build. Local implementation and conformance evidence exists, but no package, registry, production login, public SDK repository, or Pages promotion is authorized.

Preview the workflow (/docs/getting-started/)

Inspect the verified manager interface for one profile, reversible host setup, and local diagnostics.

Build against MCP (/docs/mcp/)

Use the candidate-bound two-tool contract over one long-lived stdio process.

Check what passed (/docs/evidence/)

Separate locally verified milestones from platform holds and protected production gates.

Choose a path

- Agent user: read Getting started (/docs/getting-started/); the commands are an interface preview until a protected release is approved.

- Application developer: begin with Integrations (/docs/integrations/), then use the persistent MCP contract (/docs/mcp/).

- Operator: use Operations (/docs/operations/) for separate configuration, credential, package, and vault lifecycles.

- Security or privacy reviewer: read Security (/docs/security/), Privacy (/docs/privacy/), and the machine-readable staging evidence (/staging-evidence.json).

- Agent crawler: start at llms.txt (/llms.txt) or the expanded llms-full.txt (/llms-full.txt).

# Getting started

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/getting-started/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

The verified manager creates or imports one local profile, previews an owner-marked host change, applies it with confirmation, and can remove exactly what it owns.

Interface preview, not an install command. No package is public. The local DX-06 archive uses a test-only signature and a pre-auth manager, so it must be regenerated and reverified after the final auth-merged manager hash exists.

1. Install after protected promotion

The intended package contains the public manager and proprietary engine object code without engine source. License grants, an engine EULA, production signing, registry credentials, supported-target evidence, and a separate publication approval are still required.

2. Initialize a profile

kaleidoscope --engine /absolute/path/to/kscope init --profile default --root /absolute/path/to/user-owned/kaleidoscope-memory
kaleidoscope --engine /absolute/path/to/kscope config --json

The no-argument friendly path is also implemented locally. A profile is selected through the manager and native profile registry; agent configuration receives mcp --profile NAME, not credentials or raw vault coordinates.

3. Preview and connect a host

kaleidoscope connect codex --profile default --project "$PWD" --dry-run
kaleidoscope connect codex --profile default --project "$PWD"
kaleidoscope --engine /absolute/path/to/kscope doctor --project "$PWD"

Local tests cover codex, claude, cursor, and opencode transforms. That is configuration evidence, not live acceptance by a released host version. Existing unrelated configuration is preserved; ambiguous, symlinked, tampered, or concurrently edited files are refused.

4. Verify the contract

The local candidate contract is bound to engine SHA-256 988192ac9677… and public-contract SHA-256 a2357ed6c00e…. It publishes exactly remember and search; the launch descriptor presents the agent-facing order search, remember. Ranked search returns selected_hits; addressed search returns the memory at top level.

5. Disconnect safely

kaleidoscope disconnect codex --project "$PWD" --dry-run
kaleidoscope disconnect codex --project "$PWD"

Disconnect removes only Kaleidoscope-owned material and leaves other host settings and vault bytes unchanged.

---

# Concepts and boundaries

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/concepts/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

The important boundary is local memory versus account metadata—not merely “logged in versus logged out.”

Local engine

The proprietary native engine owns the memory algorithm, canonical vault, graph, ranking, and stdio MCP behavior. Its source is not part of the public manager, client, integration, or skill surfaces.

Manager and profile

The manager initializes profiles, validates the engine launch descriptor, edits harness configuration safely, runs offline diagnostics, and installs agent guidance. The separate DX-05B candidate adds account commands and native credential storage, but it has not yet been rebound into a final distribution.

Harness identity

Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, framework clients, and generic MCP clients are consumers of the same profile. They do not become separate memory stores merely because their configuration formats differ.

Account identity

Login is designed to link a product account and device. The account protocol rejects memory fields and absolute local paths before transport. Logout or unlinking is not a vault operation and must not be interpreted as consent to upload memory.

Hosted memory

A hosted service is a later product requiring separate authorization, tenant isolation, retention, residency, deletion, sync, billing, and incident-response contracts. It is not available; login does not opt a user into it.

---

# CLI reference

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/cli/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

The developer-facing CLI is kaleidoscope. The engine executable kscope remains a native runtime/operator surface and is not the manager quickstart.

Candidate-generated reference. The exact help snapshot comes from local auth-manager commit 048bf908…. It is not a public-installation claim and will be regenerated from the final packaged manager before promotion.

Download the exact candidate help text (/reference/kaleidoscope-cli.candidate.txt).

Local memory and host commands

kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] init [--root PATH] [--profile NAME] [--durability process-local|durable-local]
kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] profile list|show|use|remove
kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] config [--profile NAME] [--json]
kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] connect HOST [--scope user|project] [--profile NAME] [--project PATH] [--opencode-version stable-v1|beta-v2] [--dry-run] [--yes]
kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] disconnect HOST [--scope user|project] [--project PATH] [--dry-run] [--yes]
kaleidoscope instructions install|remove skill|agents|claude|cursor [--project PATH] [--dry-run] [--yes]
kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] doctor [--project PATH]

Account and device commands

kaleidoscope login [--device]
kaleidoscope status [--json]
kaleidoscope logout [--all-devices] [--local-only]
kaleidoscope account link PROVIDER
kaleidoscope account unlink EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_UUID
kaleidoscope account revoke
kaleidoscope devices list
kaleidoscope devices revoke DEVICE_UUID

These account commands are locally implemented and tested but intentionally fail with provider not configured without approved issuer, audience, client, and account-origin configuration. No production issuer is published.

Safety invariants

- Mutating host and instruction commands support an effect-free dry run and explicit confirmation.

- Unknown, conflicting, symlinked, tampered, or concurrently changed targets fail closed.

- Backups are bounded and owner receipts make removal idempotent.

- Agent launch configuration contains no tokens, provider keys, or raw vault coordinates.

- Account traffic is closed to an exact account-only route inventory; it is separate from engine MCP traffic.

# MCP reference

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/mcp/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

The candidate public contract publishes exactly two model-callable MCP tools over stdio revision 2025-11-25. Everything else remains outside the agent tool list.

Exact local binding. Engine 988192ac9677…, public contract a2357ed6c00e…, macOS arm64 only. This is contract and functional evidence, not a production signature or availability claim.

Download the machine-readable candidate MCP reference (/reference/kaleidoscope-mcp.candidate.json).

search

Supply exactly one of query or memory_id. A query performs ranked retrieval and records an exposure; ledger accepts only true. Use a small protocol-defining top_k (normally about 5) and a bounded maximum_context_bytes. Ranked results appear under selected_hits. An addressed read returns the memory at top level and refuses ranking controls.

{"query":"What constraints govern the release?","top_k":5,"ledger":true}

remember

mode is required and is create, update, or delete. Create/update content begins with an H1 and carries a semantic delta with a required title and at least one fact. Every fact endpoint is declared with n, kind, and the required is gloss. Predicates are snake_case. Update/delete use memory_id and expected_version_id. Batching accepts at most 20 creates and does not share semantic fields between items.

Lifecycle

Clients keep one stdio process alive across calls, negotiate MCP once, enforce a startup deadline, cancel cleanly, bound stderr, and tear down without an orphan. DX-07 locally verifies persistent Python and TypeScript sessions; framework integrations do not run a second hidden retrieval.

Not agent tools

Feedback, lifecycle/import, maintenance, ontology, and diagnostics are controller/operator operations. Public search does not return the handle required for feedback, so there is no supported public agent-attribution path. Historical names are documented only on the migration page (/docs/migration/).

Use the manager so dry runs, backups, receipts, tamper checks, and exact removal remain intact.

# Local operations

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/operations/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Configuration, agent instructions, account credentials, installed executables, and canonical vault data have separate lifecycles.

Locate before changing

Use the manager profile and doctor views to identify the active package and profile without printing tokens or raw memory content. Never assume a worktree carries gitignored vault data.

Back up and restore

Back up the canonical vault from the main checkout or another explicit data location, not a disposable worktree. Restore only through the verified export/import path for the same supported vault format.

Disconnect and uninstall

Disconnect removes only manager-owned host configuration. Instruction removal is separate. A future installer uninstall removes package artifacts according to its scope; account logout/revocation is also separate. None of these operations implicitly deletes a vault.

Delete a vault

Vault deletion is a separate preview-and-confirm operation tied to one exact resolved root. Logical memory deletion and physical vault deletion are different operations. A broad path, unresolved variable, or ambiguous target must be refused.

Update and rollback

DX-06 locally rehearsed install, update, rollback, and uninstall under an explicitly marked staging root. It verified a test-only Ed25519 signature and a simulated update that reused the same binaries. This is not a production installer, notarization result, or supported update channel. The external vault canary remained byte-identical.

Package shapes

Local macOS arm64 staging produced an object-code archive, npm meta/platform tarballs, and Python facade/native wheels, plus aggregate SBOM and provenance. Nothing was published; other platform entries are refusal-only scaffolds.

---

# Security

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/security/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Kaleidoscope protects source distribution and establishes verifiable boundaries. A native binary remains inspectable and may be reverse engineered; object-code distribution is not a claim of impossibility.

Local engine boundary

The generated candidate contract declares a local vault, stdio MCP, no required network, and no external model calls. The manager launches the engine with a closed non-secret environment instead of inheriting provider keys, account tokens, cloud credentials, or direct vault-coordinate variables.

Account boundary

The DX-05B manager constructs only 11 declared account routes. Its request privacy guard rejects memory/profile field families and absolute local paths before transport. The provider remains unconfigured and no production account endpoint is available.

Package integrity

DX-06 binds object-code digests, source commits, bundled model, CycloneDX SBOM, provenance, candidate public contract, target, and prior-manifest rollback identity. Its signature is from a checked-in test fixture and the native code is only ad hoc/linker signed. Production trust roots, role keys, Apple signing/notarization, EULA, notices, and approved licenses are absent.

Verified privacy checks

The candidate contains no bounded private builder-path hits and no Mach-O debug sections. Local conformance used canary values for environment, outputs, profiles, host configuration, and MCP traffic. These are scoped test results, not a universal absence claim.

Report a vulnerability

Do not publish an exploit or sensitive report in a public issue. The production security contact and supported-version policy are release blockers and will be published here and in /.well-known/security.txt before promotion.

---

# Privacy and data boundary

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/privacy/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Local memory and account identity are separate systems. Logging in does not authorize memory upload, sync, analysis, training, or deletion.

Local memory data

Memory content, queries, selected results, memory IDs, graph data, local paths, vault coordinates, workspace/principal/journal identity, and local provider credentials remain engine-side fields. They are excluded from the account protocol.

Account data

The local auth candidate sends bounded account and device fields needed for OIDC login, refresh, account status, external-identity linking, logout/revocation, and device management. Device display fields reject absolute-path forms. The exact production provider, policy, retention, recovery, and account-deletion terms are not configured.

Credential storage

The native implementation uses macOS Keychain on the only natively tested platform. Windows Credential Manager and Linux Secret Service implementations exist but still need native runners. There is no plaintext credential fallback. Agent configuration and profiles do not contain refresh tokens.

Network and telemetry

The local engine contract declares no required network and no external model calls. Non-auth manager operations are offline. Account commands are the only planned account-network surface. No production telemetry inventory, destination list, consent policy, or privacy terms have been approved, so production login remains disabled.

Hosted service

Hosted memory is a future, separately authorized product. It requires explicit contracts for tenant isolation, retention, residency, deletion, sync, training use, billing, and incidents. It is not implied by these local docs.

---

# Account and devices

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/account/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Login is intended for product-account and device workflows. It is not a hosted-memory connection and is not usable against a production issuer today.

Locally verified manager flows

DX-05B commit 048bf908… implements authorization code with PKCE and a loopback callback plus device authorization for headless environments. It validates OIDC discovery, JWKS and RSA ID tokens; rotates refresh-token families; and fails closed on reuse.

Commands

kaleidoscope login
kaleidoscope login --device
kaleidoscope status --json
kaleidoscope logout
kaleidoscope logout --all-devices
kaleidoscope logout --local-only
kaleidoscope account link PROVIDER
kaleidoscope account unlink EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_UUID
kaleidoscope account revoke
kaleidoscope devices list
kaleidoscope devices revoke DEVICE_UUID

--local-only deliberately warns that it does not revoke the remote session. Without approved provider configuration, account commands return provider not configured; the docs do not provide substitute endpoints.

What logout changes

Logout removes or revokes account credentials according to scope. It does not change local profile identity or vault bytes. Vault deletion is a separate explicit local operation.

Control plane status

The client contract is closed and account-only, but production identity-provider metadata, service deployment, credentials, domains, privacy terms, recovery, and deletion procedures remain gated. No production-login claim is made.

# Benchmarks and evidence

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/benchmarks/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Benchmark results are meaningful only when the candidate, public contract, dataset, evaluator, and retrieval path are immutable and auditable.

Current result: functional smoke, no score. Benchmark PRs 3 and 4 are merged. The ordinary suite passed 20 tests with the live lane skipped; the opt-in macOS arm64 lane then passed against engine 988192ac9677… and contract a2357ed6c00e…. It deliberately records signature_verified: false.

What the live smoke proves

Before vault work it checks both digests, loads the bundled model contract, creates a fresh isolated profile and vault, discovers runtime memory types, writes one explicit semantic delta, performs ranked and addressed search, and validates the closed launch descriptor.

What it does not prove

It records no BEAM score, runs no LLM evaluator, verifies no production signature, and makes no release-readiness claim. Full ingest, answer, judge, and report phases still require the dataset, evaluator credentials, preregistered procedure, and a signed packaged candidate.

Protocol rules

The harness performs one model-facing search, records explicit top_k and maximum_context_bytes, obtains vocabulary from the runtime, isolates conversations and candidate-bound caches, and refuses stale cross-candidate phase artifacts.

Public repository

The benchmark harness is the only milestone here already merged into its public repository. That does not make the private engine, unpublished clients, staged packages, or these docs public.

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/troubleshooting/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Start with kaleidoscope doctor for local profile/engine/host issues. Account commands have a separate error boundary.

The host cannot find the tools

- Confirm the active profile and exact candidate/package digest are valid.

- Preview the host connection and inspect only the manager-owned block.

- Restart the host after a successful connect.

- Confirm the discovered tools are exactly search and remember.

OpenCode configuration is refused

Stable and beta-v2 shapes differ. The manager adopts an unambiguous existing shape or an explicit version selection; it never silently migrates stable configuration to beta. Remove conflicting duplicate Kaleidoscope entries and retry the dry run.

A profile points to the wrong place

Do not edit the profile by hand. Import the intended existing vault or initialize an explicit new root. A missing or invalid root is refused rather than created implicitly.

Login says provider not configured

That is the expected staging result: no production account origin, issuer, audience, or client ID is published. Do not invent endpoints or delete/recreate the local vault. Account status and local memory are separate.

I cannot install the package

No public installation channel exists. The local archive, npm tarballs, and wheels are evidence artifacts created with a test-only signature, not downloadable releases.

Before sharing diagnostics

Remove local paths, account identifiers, provider keys, tokens, memory content, queries, results, and vault coordinates. Use the redacted doctor artifact intended for support.

---

# Migration from historical tool contracts

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/docs/migration/
Release: unreleased
Updated: 2026-08-22

Current agents discover exactly search and remember. Historical names are not aliases and must be removed from host allowlists and prompts.

Retrieval

Replace recall, compile, and read_memory with search. Send query for ranked retrieval and memory_id for an addressed read. Ranked results are under selected_hits. Use top_k, not limit.

Writing

Replace ingest_memory or prose-inference paths with explicit remember semantic deltas. The runtime does not infer entities, facts, relationships, or dates from prose.

Other retired names

Remove merge_verdict, ontology_proposal, policy, policy_patch, ope, and replay from agent definitions. The generated candidate contract marks them retired.

Operator feedback

feedback is an operator command, not an MCP tool. Public search does not return its required decision handle, so a model has no supported public path to call it. Do not reconstruct private state or advertise a fake attribution workflow.

# Public agent skill

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/SKILL.md
SHA-256: c688db1b84ee20b6786d6109c68fbf8a21fd87486b9fe37e525d85170b77c9ad

---
# >>> kaleidoscope-manager owner=kaleidoscope-manager-v1 instruction=skill
name: use-kaleidoscope
description: Use Kaleidoscope's local memory to retrieve relevant prior context and persist verified durable decisions, preferences, constraints, corrections, procedures, relationships, and outcomes during nontrivial tasks.
---

# Use Kaleidoscope

Use the connected local Kaleidoscope MCP server as a compact continuity layer. It is not a transcript store, a substitute for repository inspection, or authority to expand the user's task.

## Public boundary

The agent-facing server publishes exactly two tools: `search` and `remember`.

- Use `search` for ranked retrieval at task start or an addressed read when the tool schema supports one.
- Use `remember` to create or correct a verified durable semantic delta.
- Do not attempt controller-only operations through MCP. The public search response does not expose the authenticated attribution handle those operations would require.
- Do not construct direct vault-coordinate commands. The selected native profile owns the root, workspace, principal, and journal coordinates outside host configuration.

If the tools are unavailable or unauthenticated, continue the user's task without fabricating memory operations.

## Retrieve

At the beginning of a nontrivial task, issue one bounded search for the decisions, preferences, constraints, procedures, relationships, or outcomes that could change the work. Prefer a compact query describing the actual goal and its important nouns over a broad request for everything.

Search again only after a material goal change, a contradiction, or evidence that the initial selection is stale or incomplete. Treat retrieved memories as fallible context: reconcile them with the user's current instructions and observable repository state. The current user request wins when they conflict.

A ranked search records the exposure associated with what it returns. Do not duplicate that record through unsupported operator calls.

## Persist durable deltas

After each user message and verified milestone, check whether the work produced a durable delta that a later task would otherwise need to rediscover. Good candidates include:

- an accepted product or architecture decision;
- a clearly stated user preference or constraint;
- a correction to prior durable context;
- a reusable procedure with a proven outcome;
- an attributable implementation or evaluation outcome backed by tests or another observable result.

Do not store tentative brainstorming, secrets, credentials, tokens, transcripts, ordinary file contents, generated logs, or claims that have not been verified. A definitive user statement is evidence for their preference or decision; an implementation claim requires observable evidence.

Keep independently correctable deltas separate. Connect them with facts when the relationship matters instead of merging unrelated claims merely to reduce tool calls.

## Follow the live write schema

Treat the connected `remember` tool schema as the authority for allowed memory types, fields, and bounds. Do not copy a vocabulary from prose or invent unsupported fields.

For a semantic delta:

- provide its required title and content in the shape published by the tool;
- express relationships as facts with subject, predicate, and object;
- declare every fact entity with a concise `is` gloss used for matching;
- propose a genuinely new predicate only when the live schema supports it, including its meaning and endpoint kinds;
- resolve dates into the supported time fields and grains rather than making dates into entities;
- use the schema's update form when correcting an existing memory instead of writing a contradictory duplicate.

Batch only related candidates when bounded batch fields are present. Never omit a known relationship just because the vocabulary is dynamic.

## Finish

Before handing off, make one final delta check. Persist only newly verified durable knowledge; do not write a ceremonial task summary when no durable delta exists.
# <<< kaleidoscope-manager owner=kaleidoscope-manager-v1 instruction=skill

# Candidate CLI help

URL: https://memory.kleosresearch.xyz/reference/kaleidoscope-cli.candidate.txt
Source: local auth-manager commit 048bf90854a1e38a1b88d14de88b681a206e5790

Kaleidoscope public local manager

Usage:
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] init [--root PATH] [--profile NAME]
                                      [--durability process-local|durable-local]
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] profile list
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] profile show NAME
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] profile use NAME
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] profile remove NAME
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] config [--profile NAME] [--json]
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] connect HOST [--scope user|project]
                                      [--profile NAME] [--project PATH]
                                      [--opencode-version stable-v1|beta-v2]
                                      [--dry-run] [--yes]
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] disconnect HOST [--scope user|project]
                                      [--project PATH] [--dry-run] [--yes]
  kaleidoscope instructions install TARGET [--project PATH] [--dry-run] [--yes]
  kaleidoscope instructions remove TARGET [--project PATH] [--dry-run] [--yes]
  kaleidoscope [--engine PATH] doctor [--project PATH]
  kaleidoscope login [--device]
  kaleidoscope status [--json]
  kaleidoscope logout [--all-devices] [--local-only]
  kaleidoscope account link PROVIDER
  kaleidoscope account unlink EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_UUID
  kaleidoscope account revoke
  kaleidoscope devices list
  kaleidoscope devices revoke DEVICE_UUID
  kaleidoscope --version

Instruction TARGET is skill, agents, claude, or cursor.
The manager edits host configuration only after preview and confirmation.
Project scope is the default. Use --dry-run for an effect-free plan.
